newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares close lower, end 1996 on sober note.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares close lower, end 1996 on sober note.

text.p: The Christmas spirit failed to enthuse share prices at Bombay bourses on Tuesday, as the market ended the last trading day of 1996 with a small loss.
The Bombay Stock Exchange's (BSE) top 30-share index closed 6.25 points, or 0.20 percent, lower at a provisional 3,086.79, off its intra-day high of 3,093.04.
Select stocks however, flared up on the back of heavy short-covering at the National Stock Exchange (NSE) on hectic volumes, traders said.
"Speculators really had a wild time today," said a dealer at a local brokerage.
ITC shot up 19.75 rupees, or 6.5 percent, to 324 at the NSE, the day's highest mark at close in volumes of over 7.7 million shares.
The share finished up 3.0 rupees at 306 at the BSE. Propped by by short-covering, MTNL surged 5.55 rupees to 244.50 on the NSE. The stock closed at 237.0 rupees at the Bombay bourse.
The BSE and most other bourses close for Christmas holidays from Wednesday. The BSE re-opens on January 1.
Under revised holidays, the NSE said it will open for trade on Thursday, close on Friday and re-open on December 31.
TELCO lost 2.0 rupees to 337.0, BSES 1.0 to 206.50, M&M 4.25 to 330.75 and BHEL 10.70 to 209.0. However, SBI rose 1.25 to 226.25, TISCO 0.75 to 164.0 and Reliance 1.50 to 203.25.
Despite an eight percent rally in the last week, the Bombay index is down one percent year-on-year from 3,110.49 on December 22, 1995 the last trading day of last year.

A disappointing annual budget, liquidity crunch in the first few months of the year, fears of political uncertainty and poor corporate earnings in the six months ending September 30, have contributed to a dismal stock market performance this year.
